message.content:
At a pressure of **10 kPa** (≈ 0.1 atm), water’s freezing point is **about –2 °C**.  

This is slightly below the normal 0 °C freezing point at 1 atm because the melting temperature of ice decreases with decreasing pressure. At 10 kPa the phase diagram of water shows the solid–liquid equilibrium line crossing the temperature axis near –2 °C.  

So, if you cool liquid water down to roughly –2 °C while maintaining a pressure of 10 kPa, it will begin to freeze.
